newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
POLITICAL PATCH-UP CHANCES RECEDE

With both the United Front (UF) and the Congress party refusing to climb down, chances of reaching a compromise before the April 11 vote of confidence receded. Prime minister Deve Gowda, readying himself for a nationally televised debate in the lower house on April 11, refused to make way for another candidate to lead the UF before Friday next. He also directed UF constituents to issue whips to their members to be present in the House on April 10. The president, who met leaders of both sides in the past week, was learnt to have advised them to find an amicable settlement to avoid a snap poll in the interest of the country.
The Hindustan Times
BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY TO STAKE CLAIM

For the first time since the crisis of survival hit the government, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) stated it would stake claim to form a new government only if it was in a position to form a stable government. It also announced it would vote out the government but is yet to decide finally on its strategy if the confidence motion comes up for a vote on April 11 as scheduled.
The Economic Times
TALKS TO END TRUCKERS' STRIKE RESUME

Talks resumed between the striking truckers and the government to end the indefinite stir. The strike has affected wholesale trade activity to the tune of 60 billion rupees with coal, steel, cement and essential commodities' supplies badly affected. Economic activity worth about 12.5 billion rupees is being affected daily.
APEX BANK LOWERS YIELD TO MATURITY

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to fix the yield to maturity (YTM) on 10-year paper at 13.56 percent for purposes of valuation of banks investment portfolio for 1996/97 (April-March). This is lower than the previous year's 14 percent. Bankers estimate this would enable them to write back nearly 18 billion rupees of the previous year's provisions.
STATE BANK TARGETS 200 BLN PROJECT EXPOSURE

The State Bank of India (SBI) is drawing up plans to raise its exposure in project finance to 200 billion rupees or 25 percent of its total assets, within the next four years. It has also decided to defer its plans to enter insurance until the lucrative life and non-life sectors are opened up. SBI has plans to enter the long term finance market in an aggressive manner.
POWERGRID PLANS 130 BLN RUPEE INVESTMENT IN 1997-2002
PowerGrid, the state-owned transmission company, would invest 130 billion rupees during 1997-2002. The decision has come in the wake of the World Bank's endorsement of its stable financial position.
Financial Express
INFLATION SLIPS TO 7.51 PER CENT

The inflation rate receded further for the second consecutive week by 0.14 percent to 7.51 percent during the week ended March 22, while maintaining its single digit streak for 104 weeks in row. It was 7.65 percent in the preceding week. This was the longest period of single digit inflation and it had broken the 1993 record when it stood in single digit for 52 weeks in succession since April 1, 1995.
TORRENT-SANOFI VENTURE TO INVOLVE ROYALTY PAYMENT

The 50:50 joint venture between Sanofi Pharma of France and the 10-billion-rupee Torrent group would involve a payment of royalty by both partners on products licensed to the new venture. Though both partners were unwilling to disclose the exact percentage of royalty payable on sales, sources indicated it would be five percent. In Torrent's case, the royalty payment would also compensate the company for transfer of key drugs group flagship Torrent Pharmaceuticals to the venture.
Business Standard
INTRANSIGENT FARMERS THREATEN FOOD SECURITY

The wheat growers' belligerent posture on the procurement price issue does not fare well for the country's food security and economy. Wheat reserves, which fell below the food security norm, would have to be replenished. However, farmers seemed in no mood to sell their produce to the government, even at the revised procurement price. The farmers made it clear they would boycott the official procurement agencies unless the minimum support price was raised.
FIs' STALL SURETY FOR FOREIGN CURRENCY LOANS

Financial institutions (FIs) decided against offering guarantees for foreign currency loans raised by small and medium corporates. The move was a result of the finance ministry rejecting the FIs' plea to close down the central bank's $3 million automatic clearances window for external commercial borrowings.
PEPSI PROPOSAL TO INJECT $155 MILLION APPROVED

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) approved PepsiCo's proposal to invest an additional $155 million into its Indian subsidiary. However, Pepsi would have to wait for clearance from the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment (CCFI). The CCFI would consider its new proposal along with the FIPB's recommendations on the former's recent query to Pepsi whether the company would be willing to divest up to 49 percent of its equity stake in downstream ventures.
The Observer
PRICES SOAR AS TRUCK STIR CONTINUES

Prices of essential commodities continued to soar as the indefinite nationwide strike by transporters entered its sixth day. Reports from Orissa said the strike was partially withdrawn, following discussions between the state government and striking truck owners. Movement of vehicles carrying essential commodities would be permitted and the state government would suspend collection of 500 rupees from outside vehicles at the border check gates. Meanwhile, the All India Motor Transport Congress, which was spearheading the stir, toughened its stand further.
Business Line
RETHINK ON AUTONOMY FOR BANKS

The government is reconsidering the proposal to grant autonomy to consistently profit-making state-owned banks in several areas. Officials of the Banking Division of the ministry of finance said there was an emerging view in the ministry that categorisation of this sort might have an adverse impact on banks which were not classified as consistently profit-making. One of the dangers would be that it might affect the credit-worthiness of the weaker banks in the market, they said.
